bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 12156, section on women known by kunya) identifies her as the wife of Ka'b b. Malik and mother of his children, among them 'Abd al-Rahman. It says Abu Musa (al-Madini) mentioned her on the authority of Ja'far but transmitted nothing from her.

It cites a report from the hadith collection of Abu Rawq al-Hamdani, via Yahya b. Abi Kathir from Muhammad b. 'Abd al-Rahman b. Thawban from Sa'd b. Zurara) points to this one. The main report attributed to him concerns the Night Journey and is transmitted via Abu Kathir al-Ansari, collected by Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shayba, al-Bazzar, al-Baghawi, Ibn al-Sakan and al-Hakim. The entry notes disagreement over whether he counts as a companion.

Ibn Hajar compares the differing chains given by Ibn Manda, Yunus b. Bukayr and Abu Nu'aym, and concludes that depending on which version is sound he is either a companion or the report is mursal.

It quotes Ibn al-Sakan that he, like his brothers 'Umara and 'Amr, was a companion but has no narration. Ibn Sa'd (via al-Baghawi) reports he was present at the Pledge of Ridwan and later events.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 331, one of his additions) says earlier compilers omitted him from the companions. Ibn Hajar argues he was a companion because his son Safwan b. Aws, husband of 'Amra bint Abi Ayyub al-Ansari, is a known tabi'i; Safwan's mother Na'ila bint al-Rabi' b. Qays gave the pledge. He reasons this shows Aws died after the Prophet, since no Ansari in Medina stayed an unbeliever in the Prophet's lifetime.

Thabit b. al-Mundhir, and the mistake came from a misreading of the name chain.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5107) lists him as a Khazraji Ansari, brother of Hassan. It quotes al-Suddi's Tafsir that he died in the Prophet's lifetime leaving a wife and five brothers who took his estate without giving her anything; she complained to the Prophet and the inheritance verse was revealed. Ibn Hajar adds that he found this only in al-Suddi and that genealogists do not list a brother of Hassan named 'Abd al-Rahman.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 11071, vol. 8 p. 92, under the name Hawwa') covers Umm Bujayd al-Ansariyya. It says Malik transmitted her hadith via Zayd ibn Aslam, 'Turn away the beggar even with a burnt hoof', and that Ahmad recorded it in his Musnad. The kunya section of the same work (entry 11908) calls her al-Ansariyya al-Harithiyya and says she is well known by her kunya. No death year is given.
research_evidence: أم بجيد، بموحدة وجيم مصغرا. روى حديثها مالك عن زيد بن أسلم، عن أم بجيد الأنصارية، عن جدتها، عن النبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلّم

full: Umm Hani'/Umm Qays al-Ansariyya
full_name_ar: أم هانئ الأنصارية ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 12290, vol. 8 p. 486) lists Umm Hani' al-Ansariyya, quoting Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr). It gives her hadith, transmitted by Durra bint Mu'adh, in which she asked the Prophet whether the dead visit one another, and he said souls become birds clinging to trees until the Day of Resurrection. It notes the hadith was recorded by Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Khaythama, al-Tabarani and Ibn Manda. No death year and no other name (such as Umm Qays) is given.

Abu 'Umar is quoted elsewhere as saying companionship is not established for 'Abd al-Rahman, Zayd or Sa'id. No death year is given.

full: 'Ammara bin al-Walid b. al-Mughira b. 'Abdullah b. 'Umar b. Makhzum b. Yaqazah b. Murrah
full_name_ar: عمارة بن الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: The page says he was born in Mecca, son of al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and brother of Khalid ibn al-Walid. It states Quraysh offered him to Abu Talib in exchange for the Prophet, and that he went to Abyssinia with 'Amr ibn al-'As to bring back the Muslim emigrants, dying there. Citing al-Isaba of Ibn Hajar and Nasab Quraysh, it says he died a non-Muslim.

full: Fatima bint al-Aswad bin 'Abd al-Asad b. Hilal b. 'Abdullah b. 'Umar b. Makhzum b. Yaqazah b. Murrah
full_name_ar: فاطمة بنت الأسود بن عبد الأسد ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Entry 11589 of al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba by Ibn Hajar gives her father as Abu al-Asad, or al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Asad. Quoting Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr), it says she is the woman on whom the Prophet carried out the penalty for theft, and to whom his words to Usama ibn Zayd, 'Do you intercede in one of Allah's prescribed penalties?', refer.
